reasons: Lake identity verifies United States v. Eric Lundin in the U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Circuit, decided 2016-03-22.
Lake citations list official citation 817 F.3d 1151 and vendor-neutral citations 2016 WL 1104851 and 2016 U.S. App. LEXIS 5236.

defect.problem: The disclosed Lundin opinion and lake record support a knock-and-talk holding, but they do not verify the stronger role label that the case illustrates a circuit split.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the role to a supportable Lundin-specific label such as "Limits knock-and-talk by time and purpose," or disclose and inventory the out-of-circuit authorities needed to prove a circuit split.

reasons: The opinion discusses Jardines and a possible issue with Ninth Circuit precedent in Vaneaton, but the disclosed opinion text does not establish a split among circuits.
The content page mentions Walker and Carloss, but no lake records or opinion text for those cases are disclosed for this assertion.
residual_risks: The circuit-split label may be true from outside authorities, but it is not verifiable from the disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use a narrower role grounded in Lundin itself unless supporting split authorities are added.

reasons: The opinion states that officers violated the Fourth Amendment when they knocked at 4:00 a.m. without a warrant and with intent to arrest Lundin, and that the immediately ensuing search was illegal.
The opinion gives two reasons the officers exceeded the customary license: normal waking-hours limits and purpose limits tied to asking questions rather than arresting.
The opinion states that the unlawful knock caused the crashing noises, so those noises could not justify the search that produced the handguns.
The opinion treats the front porch as curtilage, calling it the classic exemplar of curtilage under Jardines.
The knock-and-talk analysis turns on whether officers lawfully occupied the curtilage, so a Curtilage cross-doctrine role is supported.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: A more precise role would be "Applies curtilage doctrine to front-porch knock-and-talk."
